cards.hypothesis: Subjects with high baseline heart rate variability (HRV) exhibit non-exchangeable residuals under Mondrian binning by stress condition, causing conditional coverage failure
cards.proposed_mechanism: High baseline HRV subjects have wider residual distributions within each Mondrian bin (stress condition), but the conformal quantile is computed globally per bin, leading to systematic undercoverage for these subjects
cards.causal_path: High baseline HRV → increased within-bin residual variance → fixed per-bin quantile too narrow → undercoverage
control_variables: include age and fitness as covariates in residual modeling
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is driven by sensor noise artifacts during stress transitions, not baseline HRV
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with motion artifact magnitude during condition transitions, not with baseline HRV
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress per-subject coverage deficit on baseline_rmssd controlling for transition_artifact_index; significant baseline_rmssd coefficient supports H1
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior WESAD analyses show baseline HRV explains ~15-20% variance in stress reactivity; expect similar magnitude for coverage deficit
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in top baseline_rmssd tertile show coverage deficit >5% vs nominal; bottom tertile shows deficit <2%
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between baseline_rmssd and per-subject coverage deficit after controlling for transition artifacts
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_deficit ~ baseline_rmssd + transition_artifact_index + (1|subject), test baseline_rmssd coefficient
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with subject-specific quantiles per bin; if undercoverage persists for high-HRV subjects, mechanism is falsified

cards.hypothesis: Wrist EDA sensor drift during prolonged stress condition creates non-stationary residuals that violate exchangeability within Mondrian bins
cards.proposed_mechanism: EDA baseline wander accumulates over the 10-min stress task, shifting residual distribution rightward within the stress bin; early-calibration quantiles undercover late-task predictions
cards.causal_path: Prolonged stress → EDA baseline drift → residual distribution shift within stress bin → fixed quantile too low for late windows → undercoverage
control_variables: detrend EDA per subject per condition
control for temperature via TEMP sensor
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from individual differences in stress recovery speed, not sensor drift
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with post-stress recovery time constant, not with within-stress EDA drift rate
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage in first vs last stress window; H2 predicts deficit increases with window_index, rival predicts no within-condition trend
cards.effect_size_rationale: EDA drift can shift baseline by 0.5-2 µS over 10 min; residual SD ~0.3 µS; expect coverage drop from 90% to <70% in late windows
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage in last stress window <80% while first window >88% for drifted subjects; drift_slope >0.05 µS/min predicts deficit
cards.failure_condition: No significant within-stress coverage decline; coverage deficit uncorrelated with eda_baseline_slope
cards.statistical_test_plan: Logistic regression: coverage_indicator ~ window_index + eda_baseline_slope + window_index:eda_baseline_slope, cluster by subject
cards.falsification_test: Apply online drift correction (Kalman filter) to EDA before conformal prediction; if undercoverage eliminated, H2 confirmed; if persists, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Subjects with delayed cortisol response (slow HPA axis) have mislabeled stress windows during early stress condition, contaminating Mondrian calibration
cards.proposed_mechanism: Slow cortisol responders show low physiological arousal in first 3 min of stress task; these windows labeled 'stress' but resemble baseline, inflating stress-bin residual variance and widening quantile, yet coverage fails for truly aroused windows
cards.causal_path: Slow HPA axis → low early-stress arousal → mislabeled low-arousal windows in stress bin → inflated stress-bin quantile → undercoverage for high-arousal windows
control_variables: exclude first 3 min of stress condition
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects genuine physiological heterogeneity in stress response patterns, not labeling error
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with response pattern cluster membership, not with cortisol_aucg or early_stress_eda
cards.distinguishing_test: Train separate Mondrian models with/without first 3 min of stress; H3 predicts coverage improves for slow responders when early windows excluded
cards.effect_size_rationale: ~30% of WESAD subjects show blunted early stress response; excluding 3/10 min windows reduces stress-bin n by 30%, expect 5-8% coverage recovery
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with cortisol_aucg < median show >10% coverage improvement when first 3 min excluded; fast responders show <2% change
cards.failure_condition: Excluding early stress windows does not differentially improve coverage for low-cortisol subjects
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired t-test per subject: coverage_full vs coverage_excl_early; regress improvement on cortisol_aucg
cards.falsification_test: Relabel early stress windows as 'baseline' using physiological clustering; retrain Mondrian; if undercoverage persists for slow responders, H3 falsified

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian taxonomy based solely on condition label ignores circadian phase, causing undercoverage for subjects tested at non-optimal circadian times
cards.proposed_mechanism: Cortisol and HRV follow circadian rhythms; subjects tested at circadian trough have compressed dynamic range, residuals cluster near zero but with heavy tails; fixed per-condition quantile misses tail events
cards.causal_path: Circadian trough testing → compressed physiological dynamic range → heavy-tailed residuals within condition bin → fixed quantile misses tails → undercoverage
control_variables: include time_of_day as Mondrian stratification variable
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to inter-subject variability in stress reactivity, not circadian phase
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with stress_reactivity_score, not with time_of_day or circadian_phase_proxy
cards.distinguishing_test: Add time_of_day bins to Mondrian taxonomy; H4 predicts coverage improves specifically for off-peak subjects, rival predicts no change
cards.effect_size_rationale: Circadian effect on HRV ~10-15% amplitude; WESAD collected 8am-6pm; expect 2-4% coverage gap between peak/trough
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects tested 8-10am show coverage >88%; subjects tested 4-6pm show coverage <82% under current taxonomy; adding time bins equalizes
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference across time_of_day bins; adding time bins does not improve worst-bin coverage
cards.statistical_test_plan: Chi-square test of coverage homogeneity across time_of_day bins; logistic regression coverage ~ sin(2π*hour/24) + cos(2π*hour/24)
cards.falsification_test: Simulate data with known circadian effect using WESAD parameters; apply Mondrian with/without time bins; if time bins don't recover coverage in simulation, H4 falsified

cards.hypothesis: Chest RESP sensor displacement during stress-induced movement creates intermittent signal loss, generating outlier residuals that violate Mondrian's exchangeability assumption
cards.proposed_mechanism: Stress causes upper body movement → chest band loosens → RESP signal drops out → imputed values create large residuals in stress bin → quantile inflated but coverage fails for clean windows due to contaminated calibration
cards.causal_path: Stress movement → chest_band_displacement → RESP_signal_loss → imputation_artifacts → contaminated stress-bin residuals → miscalibrated quantile → undercoverage
control_variables: use wrist ACC as movement proxy
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects true physiological variability in breathing patterns under stress, not sensor artifacts
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with breathing_pattern_complexity (entropy), not with chest_acc_magnitude or signal_quality
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage in stress windows with high vs low chest_acc_magnitude; H5 predicts deficit only in high-movement windows
cards.effect_size_rationale: Signal loss events create residuals 3-5× SD; even 10% contaminated windows can drop coverage from 90% to 75%
cards.testable_prediction: Windows with chest_acc_magnitude > 90th percentile show coverage <70%; low-movement windows show coverage >88%
cards.failure_condition: Coverage deficit uncorrelated with chest_acc_magnitude and resp_signal_quality
cards.statistical_test_plan: Stratified coverage test: binomial test per movement stratum; interaction test coverage ~ movement_stratum * bin
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian using only wrist sensors (EDA, ACC, BVP, TEMP); if undercoverage persists identically, chest RESP artifacts not the cause

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's fixed binning by discrete condition labels fails for subjects with graded stress responses, causing undercoverage at intermediate arousal levels
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects show continuous arousal gradients across conditions; Mondrian forces discrete bins (baseline/stress/amusement); intermediate windows get binned by label not physiology, creating heterogeneous residual distributions
cards.causal_path: Graded arousal response → label-physiology mismatch → within-bin residual bimodality → single quantile covers neither mode → undercoverage
control_variables: test adaptive binning by arousal quantiles
cards.rival_explanation: Discrete conditions are physiologically distinct; undercoverage stems from model misspecification, not binning granularity
cards.rival_prediction: Residual distributions are unimodal within each condition; coverage deficit uniform across arousal levels
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit Gaussian mixture to stress-bin residuals; H6 predicts bimodality (p<0.01 dip test); rival predicts unimodality
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD shows continuous valence/arousal gradients; expect 2-3 subpopulations in stress bin; coverage gap ~5-8% at mode boundaries
minimum_data_needed: per-window physiological features (EDA, HR, RESP, TEMP)
cards.testable_prediction: Stress-bin residuals show significant bimodality (Hartigan's dip test p<0.01); coverage <80% at arousal quantiles 0.4-0.6
cards.failure_condition: Residuals unimodal within bins; coverage deficit not concentrated at intermediate arousal
cards.statistical_test_plan: Hartigan's dip test per bin; coverage vs arousal_quantile LOESS; compare fixed vs adaptive (arousal-quantile) binning via paired bootstrap
cards.falsification_test: Replace Mondrian bins with 5 arousal-quantile bins; if undercoverage persists at same magnitude, binning granularity not the mechanism

cards.hypothesis: Subjects taking beta-blockers exhibit attenuated cardiac stress response, causing systematic undercoverage in HR-based predictions due to shifted residual distribution
cards.proposed_mechanism: Beta-blockers blunt HR increase during stress → HR residuals in stress bin shifted negative with reduced variance → conformal quantile calibrated on mixed population too wide for beta-blocker subjects → undercoverage
cards.causal_path: Beta-blocker use → blunted HR stress response → shifted stress-bin HR residual distribution → population quantile mismatched → undercoverage for medicated subjects
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for medicated subjects reflects comorbid conditions affecting autonomic regulation, not beta-blockers per se
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with comorbidity_count, not with beta_blocker_flag after adjustment
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage for beta-blocker vs non-beta-blocker subjects matched on comorbidity_count and fitness; H7 predicts deficit persists
cards.effect_size_rationale: Beta-blockers reduce HR stress reactivity by 30-50%; residual shift ~15-20 bpm; expect coverage drop from 90% to 60-70%
cards.testable_prediction: Beta-blocker subjects show stress-bin HR residual mean < -10 bpm vs > +5 bpm for controls; coverage <75% vs >88%
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference between beta-blocker and matched controls; residual distributions overlap
cards.statistical_test_plan: Propensity score matching on age/fitness/comorbidities; McNemar test for paired coverage difference; quantile regression of residuals on beta_blocker_flag
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian quantiles separately for beta-blocker subgroup; if coverage normalizes, H7 confirmed; if undercoverage persists, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Temporal autocorrelation in physiological residuals violates Mondrian's exchangeability assumption, causing undercoverage for subjects with high residual autocorrelation
cards.proposed_mechanism: Physiological signals show AR(1) structure; Mondrian treats windows as exchangeable within bin; high-autocorrelation subjects have effective sample size << nominal n, quantile estimated with false precision → undercoverage
cards.causal_path: High residual AR(1) coefficient → low effective sample size per bin → quantile estimation error → nominal coverage not achieved
control_variables: use block bootstrap for quantile estimation
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to heteroscedasticity, not autocorrelation
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with residual_variance_heterogeneity, not with residual_ar1_coefficient
cards.distinguishing_test: Re-estimate quantiles using block bootstrap (block size = 1/rho); H8 predicts coverage recovery for high-rho subjects
cards.effect_size_rationale: Typical physiological AR(1) rho=0.3-0.7; effective_n reduction 30-70%; expect 4-10% coverage deficit for rho>0.5
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with residual_ar1 > 0.5 show coverage <80%; block bootstrap quantiles restore coverage to >88%
cards.failure_condition: Coverage deficit uncorrelated with residual_ar1_coefficient; block bootstrap does not improve coverage
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation: per-subject coverage vs residual_ar1; paired test: standard vs block-bootstrap coverage per subject
cards.falsification_test: Subsample windows to eliminate autocorrelation (keep every k-th window where k > 1/rho); if undercoverage persists, autocorrelation not the cause

cards.hypothesis: Self-report stress labels in WESAD contain systematic bias for high-alexithymia subjects, contaminating Mondrian calibration bins
cards.proposed_mechanism: High alexithymia subjects underreport subjective stress → labeled 'baseline' windows actually contain stress physiology → baseline-bin residuals inflated → quantile too wide → but stress-bin quantile too narrow due to missing high-arousal windows → undercoverage for stress
cards.causal_path: High alexithymia → self-report stress underestimation → label-physiology mismatch → contaminated baseline bin + depleted stress bin → asymmetric quantile error → stress undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects true physiological non-responders, not labeling bias
cards.rival_prediction: Physiological arousal during stress condition is genuinely low for low-coverage subjects; re-labeling doesn't change coverage
cards.distinguishing_test: Cluster stress-condition windows by physiology; H9 predicts high-alexithymia subjects have 'stress-physiology' windows labeled baseline
cards.effect_size_rationale: Alexithymia prevalence ~10%; labeling error rate ~15% in high-TAS; expect 2-4% coverage impact at population level, larger in subgroup
cards.testable_prediction: High-TAS subjects (score>60) show >15% of baseline windows clustering with stress physiology; their stress-bin coverage <80%
cards.failure_condition: No label-physiology mismatch in high-TAS subjects; re-labeling by physiology doesn't improve their coverage
cards.statistical_test_plan: Gaussian mixture clustering of stress-condition windows; chi-square test of label-cluster association by TAS group; coverage comparison
cards.falsification_test: Train Mondrian on physiology-derived labels only; if undercoverage persists for high-TAS subjects, labeling bias not the mechanism

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's marginal coverage guarantee fails under covariate shift between calibration and test subjects due to WESAD's small subject pool (n=15)
cards.proposed_mechanism: With only 15 subjects, leave-one-subject-out calibration creates covariate shift: test subject's residual distribution differs from calibration pool; Mondrian's marginal guarantee doesn't protect conditional coverage for out-of-distribution subjects
cards.causal_path: Small n_subjects → high between-subject residual distribution variability → LOO calibration quantile mismatched for held-out subject → undercoverage for distributional outliers
control_variables: importance weighting by residual distribution similarity
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to within-subject non-exchangeability, not between-subject covariate shift
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficit correlates with within-subject residual non-stationarity, not with between-subject distributional distance
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute Wasserstein distance between held-out subject's calibration residuals and pool; H10 predicts coverage deficit correlates with this distance
cards.effect_size_rationale: n=15 is extremely small for distributional coverage; expect 10-20% coverage gap for outlier subjects; marginal coverage ~90% but conditional <70%
cards.testable_prediction: Top 3 Wasserstein-distance subjects show coverage <75%; bottom 3 show coverage >90%; marginal coverage across all ~90%
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between Wasserstein distance and coverage deficit; hierarchical conformal doesn't improve worst-subject coverage
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation: wasserstein_distance vs coverage_deficit; compare LOO vs hierarchical conformal via paired subject-level coverage
cards.falsification_test: Augment calibration with synthetic subjects from fitted hierarchical model; if undercoverage persists for real outliers, covariate shift not the sole mechanism
